Bug_Explanation: The issue arises from the way characters are passed into the StringBuffer and StringBuilder constructors. When a character is passed in, Java will implicitly convert it into an integer. The result is that the buffer is not only initialized with a single character, but with the integer equivalent of the character. Hence, the capacity of the StringBuffer and StringBuilder objects is larger than expected.
Trigger_Explanation: The JUnit test case triggers the bug by calling the'showBug' method in the 'Main' class. The'showBug' method contains the buggy code that creates StringBuffer and StringBuilder objects with individual character values. The result is that the buffer capacity is larger than expected.
